bug_semantics: In os/io.c ReadRequestFromClient, a Big Request's 32-bit length (CARD32 units of 4 bytes) from get_big_req_len is stored in unsigned int needed and converted to bytes with needed <<= 2 before the max-size check (historically MAXBUFSIZE, later needed > maxBigRequestSize << 2). A client-supplied length greater than UINT_MAX/4 wraps needed to a small byte count, so the bound appears to pass and the server continues with a truncated length (realloc/copy/dispatch), enabling memory corruption and DoS (CWE-190). A second identical <<= 2 after assembling a complete xBigReq has the same wrap. Local X client with Big Requests; CVSS AV:L/PR:L. Vendor (X.Org/Red Hat) rates this a real integer-overflow bypass of the size check.
flaw_origin: X.Org's 2025-06-17 advisory attributes introduction to X11R6.0 (Big Requests). In this clone the first surviving write of the multiply-then-check pattern is the 2003-11-14 Xorg R6.6 baseline import by Kaleb Keithley (ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1), which added os/io.c with get_big_req_len, needed <<= 2, then if (needed > MAXBUFSIZE) and a second needed <<= 2 after the header is completed. Immediate parent cb6ef07bf01e72d1a6e6e83ceb7f76d6534da941 is a Tiny-X/kdrive hw-only tree with no os/io.c and no get_big_req_len. Later commits (BIGREQS mandatory 2008, maxBigRequestSize substitution 2007, 2012 indent) only carried or restyled the same conversion; they did not first-write it. No finer public git member of the X11R6.0 original is reconstructable here.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: a Big Request length is multiplied by 4 (needed <<= 2) before the max-size test in ReadRequestFromClient, so a large CARD32 wraps and bypasses the check (CWE-190). CVE.org is PUBLISHED; X.Org and Red Hat treat it as a real issue, not withdrawn. BIC search used git log -L / -S / blame-as-lead on the <<= 2 sites, not an AI-commit-first search. The smallest surviving first-write in this public history is the 2003 R6.6 baseline import that added os/io.c with get_big_req_len + needed <<= 2 + post-multiply MAXBUFSIZE check; parent cb6ef07bf01e72d1a6e6e83ceb7f76d6534da941 was checked directly and lacks os/io.c. That import is a bulk baseline, but no finer public member (X11R6.0 git SHA) is reconstructable in this clone, so per protocol it is a valid BIC. Later style/mandatory-BIGREQS/maxBigRequestSize commits are not first-writes. AI judged only from that BIC commit object: human Kaleb Keithley, empty trailers, 2003 — NOT_AI. Fix is Olivier Fourdan 03731b326a80b582e48d939fe62cb1e2b10400d9 on master (direct patch of the first overflow site), with follow-up 4fc4d76b2c7aaed61ed2653f997783a3714c4fe1 for the second site; release tags 21.1.17 / 24.1.7 contain the corresponding cherry-picks and postdate the BIC.
